mainTopic: Carrying out stoning, the witnesses' hands and קרא כדכתיב, and who is hung after execution
overview: The amud opens by finishing a derivation from the doubled verb סקול יסקל. It then explains how the stoning is carried out: both witnesses lift the heavy stone, but the second witness throws it alone so it lands with force. The משנה gives the law for when all of ישראל must join in, even though in practice the first stone always killed. A new stone was prepared after each execution, because the tools are buried near the executed person. שמואל rules that if the witnesses' hands were cut off after the trial, the person is not executed, because the פסוק requires the witnesses' hand to be first. The גמרא defends this rule. The murderer and the גואל הדם may be handled 'in any way', but they are two פסוקים that teach the same thing, so they are exceptions and do not set a general rule. Proofs for קרא כדכתיב are then tried from בן סורר ומורה and from עיר הנדחת, and the גמרא concludes that the question is a dispute between תנאים, as seen in the מצורע missing a right thumb. Finally, a new משנה asks which executed people are hung after death. The גמרא begins explaining that רבי אליעזר and the חכמים read the פסוקים with different methods, כלל ופרט against ריבוי ומיעוט, and this explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The doubled verb teaches the final point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends an earlier derivation by citing the doubled verb סקול יסקל as its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'He shall surely be stoned' (סקול יסקל).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a line of questions from the lines just before this, answering the last one with the פסוק סקול יסקל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verb is doubled: 'stone, he shall be stoned.' The גמרא reads the extra word as teaching something more. Here it shows that the law of stoning applies in all places and at all times.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; introduces a source from a פסוק
He shall surely be stoned; a doubled verb that teaches an extra point

phrases.english: The verse states: "He shall surely be stoned."
phrases.notes: שמות 19:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a derivation that began before this section
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled verb סקול יסקל is the source for the law being derived.

steps.title: How can one witness take a stone that needs two men?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה saying the second witness takes the stone, then asks how, since a ברייתא says the stone needed two men to carry it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If he did not die, the second witness takes the stone.' Does he take it by himself? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: there was a stone there that needed two people to carry it. He takes it and puts it on the person's chest. If the person dies from it, the obligation is done.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line of the משנה and challenges it with a ברייתא that seems to say one person could not lift the stone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the singular 'the second witness takes' (נוטל), so it sounds like he acts alone. The ברייתא says the stone was a load for two people (משוי שני בני אדם). If the stone took two men to carry, how could one witness take it?

keyTerms.meaning: The second witness
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? Introduces a challenge from an outside source
A load for two people; too heavy for one person to carry
He has fulfilled the obligation; the execution is complete

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו, עֵד הַשֵּׁנִי נוֹטֵל אֶת הָאֶבֶן.
phrases.english: And if not, the second witness takes the stone.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה. 'If not' means if the person did not die from being pushed off the height.

phrases.english: Takes?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר,
phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says,

phrases.aramaic: אֶבֶן הָיְתָה שָׁם מַשּׂוֹי שְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם,
phrases.english: There was a stone there, a load for two people;
he takes it and places it on his chest.
phrases.notes: 'Places' here means throwing it down onto the chest of the person being executed.

phrases.english: If he died from it, the obligation is fulfilled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's wording that the second witness 'takes' the stone, which sounds like he does it alone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the stone was a load for two men, so one witness could not lift it by himself.

steps.title: The ברייתא has the same problem inside it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא contradicts itself in the same way, so the משנה's wording cannot be read too literally.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, the ברייתא itself should be hard for you: it says the stone was a load for two people, and then it says 'he takes it and places it on his chest.'
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of answering right away, the גמרא shows that the ברייתא also says 'he takes it' in the singular, right after saying the stone needed two men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'he takes' really meant 'alone,' the ברייתא would contradict itself. So the singular 'takes' must mean something else. This prepares the real explanation in the next step, which will work for both the משנה and the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning; turns the questioner's logic back on him
The source itself should be hard for you; it contradicts itself

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, the ברייתא itself should be difficult for you:
A load for two people,
and yet he takes it and places it on his chest?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the challenge by showing the ברייתא has the same problem
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading 'he takes' as 'he takes it alone'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא itself uses 'he takes' about a stone it says needed two men, so the singular verb cannot mean he acted alone.

steps.title: Both lift it, but one throws it
steps.stepSummary: Both witnesses lift the stone together, but only the second witness throws it, so it falls with force.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he lifts it together with his fellow witness, and he alone throws it, so that it comes down with force.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an explanation that fits both the משנה and the ברייתא: the lifting is done by two, the throwing by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Two people's load' describes the lifting, which both witnesses do. 'He takes it and places it' describes the throw, which the second witness does alone. Having only one person throw it makes the stone land with full force on the chest.

keyTerms.meaning: He lifts
Together with his fellow; here, the other witness
Throws
With force

steps.whatToRemember: The second witness lifts the stone together with the other witness, but he throws it alone.

phrases.english: Rather, he lifts it together with his fellow,
and he himself throws it,
so that it comes down with force.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the explanation that settles the challenge from step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the action into two parts: lifting (two people) and throwing (one person)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'He takes the stone' means the second witness handles it entirely alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both witnesses lift the stone, and the second witness alone throws it so it lands with force.

steps.title: Was a second stone ever needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה saying all of ישראל finish the stoning, and challenges it with a ברייתא saying no one ever needed to throw again.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And if not, his stoning is done by all of ישראל.' But a ברייתא teaches: no person ever had to do it a second time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and points out that a ברייתא says the first stone always killed the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes a further stage in which all of ישראל stone the person. The ברייתא says this never happened, because no one ever needed a second stone. So why does the משנה describe something that never took place?

keyTerms.meaning: His stoning
No person ever did it a second time

phrases.english: And if not, his stoning, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' stands for the rest of the משנה's line: his stoning is done by all of ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: מֵעוֹלָם לֹא שָׁנָה בָּהּ אָדָם!
phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Never did a person repeat it!
phrases.notes: The first stone always killed him, so no one ever needed to throw a second.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: מֵעוֹלָם לֹא שָׁנָה בָּהּ אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that all of ישראל complete the stoning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says no second stone was ever needed, so that stage never actually happened.

steps.title: The משנה only says what would happen if needed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is not saying this ever happened, only what the law would be if a second stone were needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did I say that they actually did it? I said that if it would be necessary, this is what is done.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is giving the law for a case that could happen, not reporting what actually happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tells us what happened in practice: the first stone always worked. The משנה tells us the law if it ever had not. These two do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Did I say...? Introduces a correction of how someone understood the statement
That if it were needed

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives the law for a case where a second stone is needed, even though in practice it never was.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the משנה and the ברייתא disagree. The ברייתא describes what happened, and the משנה gives the law for 'what if.'

phrases.english: Did I say that they did it?
I said that if it were needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separates the law in principle from what happened in practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is describing something that actually used to happen.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה states the law if a second stone were ever needed, which fits with the ברייתא saying it never was.

steps.title: Was the same stone really used every time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that 'there was a stone' at the stoning place, and challenges it with another ברייתא saying the stone is buried with the executed person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'There was a stone' at the place of stoning. But a ברייתא teaches: the stone used to stone him, the tree he was hung on, the sword used to kill him, and the cloth used to strangle him are all buried with him. So how could the same stone stay there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier ברייתא, which said a stone was kept at the stoning place. It asks how that works if the stone is buried with the dead person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'there was a stone' sound like one stone was kept and used again and again. But if every stone used in an execution gets buried, it cannot be reused. The two ברייתות seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said', used to bring back a line from a ברייתא already quoted
'But isn't it taught?', bringing a ברייתא as a challenge
They are buried with him
A cloth or scarf, used for חנק (strangling)

phrases.english: The Master said: 'There was a stone, etc.'
phrases.notes: This is the earlier ברייתא: there was a stone at the place of stoning, so heavy it took two men to carry.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Both the stone with which he was stoned,
and the tree on which he was hung,
and the sword with which he was killed,
and the cloth with which he was strangled –
all of them are buried with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: אֶבֶן הָיְתָה כּוּ׳. וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the throwing of the stone to the question of where the stone comes from.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that a stone was kept at the stoning place
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the stone is always buried with the executed person, there cannot be one permanent stone that is used again.

steps.title: A new stone was brought each time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that after each burial, they prepared and brought another stone to replace it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed to teach that they would prepare and bring other stones in place of the buried ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the stone was buried, and then a new one was brought to take its place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'There was a stone' does not mean the same stone forever. It means there was always a stone ready at the stoning place, because each buried stone was replaced. Now both ברייתות fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is only needed for...', explaining what case a teaching is really about
In their place, as replacements

phrases.english: No, it is needed
that they prepare and bring others in their place.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא דִּמְתַקְּנִי וּמַיְיתִי אַחֲרִינֵי חִלּוּפַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting one source so both can be true
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One stone was kept and reused for every stoning.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each stone was buried, and a new one was prepared to replace it.

steps.title: Are the tools buried with him or not?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא contrasts the ברייתא saying the tools are buried with him against another ברייתא saying they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They are buried with him.' But isn't it taught in another ברייתא: they are not buried with him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks closely at the words 'buried with him' and brings a different ברייתא that says the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One ברייתא says the stone, tree, sword and cloth go into the grave with the person. Another says they do not. The גמרא needs to explain this direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not buried with him

phrases.english: 'They are buried with him.'
But isn't it taught: They are not buried with him?

steps.triggerLanguage: נִקְבָּרִין עִמּוֹ. וְהָתַנְיָא: אֵין נִקְבָּרִין עִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the same ברייתא from step 7, now questioning its words 'buried with him'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase נקברין עמו in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות give opposite rulings on whether the tools are buried with the executed person.

steps.title: 'With him' means near him
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that 'with him' means within his area, near the grave, not in the same grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: What does 'with him' mean? With him, in his area.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא settles the contradiction by explaining what 'with him' really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tools are not placed in the actual grave, which is what 'not buried with him' means. But they are buried close by, in the area around his grave, which is what 'buried with him' means. So both ברייתות are right.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the question
In his area, the space around his grave

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
What does 'with him' mean?
With him, within his area.
phrases.notes: Literally 'in his grasp'. He means the ground around the grave, not inside the grave itself.

steps.whatToRemember: The execution tools are buried near the executed person, not in his grave, and a new stone is prepared for the next stoning.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מַאי עִמּוֹ? עִמּוֹ בִּתְפִיסָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining a word so the two sources do not really argue
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'With him' means inside the same grave.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'With him' means in the area near his grave.

steps.title: If the witnesses' hands were cut off, he is not executed
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that if the witnesses' hands were cut off, the person is exempt, because the פסוק requires the witnesses' hand to be first.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: If the witnesses' hands were cut off, he is exempt. Why? Because we need 'the hand of the witnesses shall be first upon him', and here that is missing.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. שמואל gives a rule about what happens if the witnesses lose their hands after the person was sentenced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the witnesses' hand must be the first to act in the execution. If they no longer have hands, this cannot be done. So the execution cannot happen at all, and the person goes free.

keyTerms.meaning: An early אמורא
Was cut off
Exempt, here meaning he is not executed
First, before anyone else
And it is not there

phrases.english: שמואל said:
If the hand of the witnesses was cut off, he is exempt.
What is the reason?
Because we need 'The hand of the witnesses shall be upon him first,'
phrases.notes: דברים 17:7

phrases.english: and that is missing.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the witnesses' part in the execution is not just a nice custom. Without it, the execution cannot happen at all.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: נִקְטְעָה יַד הָעֵדִים פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the witnesses' role in the stoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the witnesses' hands were cut off after the sentence, the person is not executed, since the פסוק requires their hand to be first.

steps.title: Would witnesses without hands be disqualified?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if so, witnesses who never had hands should not be allowed to testify at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is so, witnesses who had no hands from the start, are they also disqualified?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes שמואל's reasoning further, to see if it leads to a strange result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the witnesses must use their own hand to start the execution, then witnesses born without hands could never do it. That would mean they cannot be witnesses in such cases at all. The גמרא is asking if this is really true.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so, then...', taking an idea to its result
People without hands
From the beginning
They are disqualified

phrases.english: If that is so,
witnesses without hands from the start,
are they also disqualified?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's reason from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reason that the witnesses' hand is required
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the hand is required, witnesses who never had hands could never fulfill it, so they would have to be disqualified. That seems too far.

steps.title: The פסוק means hands they already had
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק says 'the hand of the witnesses', meaning the hand they already had when they testified.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the פסוק says 'the hand of the witnesses', meaning a hand that was already there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the פסוק more exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The hand of the witnesses' means the hand these witnesses had when they testified. If they had hands then and lost them later, the rule cannot be done, so the person goes free. If they never had hands, the פסוק is not talking about them, so they can still testify and others throw first.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is different there', showing a difference between cases
The פסוק
Already

phrases.english: It is different there,
because the verse says: 'The hand of the witnesses,'
meaning a hand that was already there.

steps.whatToRemember: Losing hands after testifying stops the execution. Witnesses who had no hands from the start can still testify.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases: hands cut off later means he is פטור, but witnesses with no hands from the start are still valid.
steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאָמַר קְרָא: יַד הָעֵדִים, שֶׁהָיְתָה כְּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exact reading of the פסוק separating the two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any witness without hands could never fulfill the פסוק, so he would be disqualified.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק only requires the hand the witnesses already had when testifying. Those who never had hands are not included in the rule and are still valid witnesses.

steps.title: A משנה seems to allow execution without the original witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל from a משנה: if two people testify that someone was already sentenced in another court, he is executed. This seems to work even when the original witnesses are not there.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: In any case where two people testify and say, 'We testify that so-and-so was sentenced in such-and-such court, and so-and-so and so-and-so were his witnesses,' he is executed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that seems to go against שמואל's rule from step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the witnesses' hand must be first, so if they cannot throw, there is no execution. The משנה says new testimony that he was already sentenced is enough to kill him, even though the original witnesses seem to be missing. So it looks like we do not need the original witnesses' hands at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a תנאי source)
So-and-so; a certain person
His verdict was finished; he was sentenced
He is executed

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Any place where two testify about him and say,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מכות 7a, about a convicted person who ran away and was found somewhere else.

phrases.english: 'We testify about so-and-so
that his sentence was finished in such-and-such court,
and so-and-so and so-and-so were his witnesses'
he is executed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to שמואל's rule after the earlier question was settled in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that if the witnesses cannot throw first, the person is exempt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows execution based on testimony about an earlier sentence, which suggests the original witnesses' hands are not needed.

steps.title: שמואל: the משנה speaks about the same witnesses
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the משנה is talking about a case where the people testifying now are the original witnesses themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל explained it as a case where they themselves are his witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the challenge by narrowing the case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the people testifying in the new court are the same witnesses from the first trial, then they are present and can throw first. So the משנה fits שמואל's rule after all.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it; he interpreted it
They themselves are his witnesses

phrases.english: שמואל explained it
as a case where they themselves are his witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to allow execution even without the original witnesses present.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about the original witnesses testifying again, so they are present to throw first.

steps.title: A murderer may be killed in any possible way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether we really must keep a פסוק exactly as written. A ברייתא teaches that if a murderer cannot be killed in his written way, he is killed in any way possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do we really need to do the פסוק exactly as written? Isn't it taught: 'The one who struck shall surely be put to death, he is a murderer.' This would only teach the death written for him. How do we know that if you cannot kill him with the death written for him, you kill him in any way you can? The פסוק says 'shall surely be put to death, the one who struck,' meaning in any way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to שמואל from a ברייתא about a murderer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל exempts the person because we cannot do 'the hand of the witnesses first' as written. But the ברייתא shows that by a murderer, when the written way cannot be done, we still kill him another way. So why not here too: let him be executed even if the witnesses cannot throw first?

keyTerms.meaning: Exactly as it is written
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא
He shall surely be put to death (the doubled word)
In any case; in any way

phrases.english: But do we need the verse exactly as it is written?
But isn't it taught:
'The one who struck shall surely be put to death, he is a murderer'
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:21

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בְּמִיתָה הַכְּתוּבָה בּוֹ.
phrases.english: I would only know this with the death written for him.
From where do we know that if you are not able
to kill him with the death written for him
that you kill him with any death
that you are able to kill him with?
The verse says: 'The one who struck shall surely be put to death'
in any way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 15 saves שמואל from the משנה, the גמרא raises a new, broader challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's idea that if a פסוק cannot be done as written, the execution falls away.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By a murderer, when the written death cannot be done, we still execute him another way, so the written details are not needed to stop the execution.

steps.title: The murderer is different because the Torah says so
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the murderer is a special case, since the פסוק itself says מות יומת to teach 'any way.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the פסוק says: 'He shall surely be put to death.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 16 by saying the murderer case is special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if a פסוק cannot be done as written, we do not change it. By a murderer, the Torah added מות יומת to tell us to kill him any way possible. Without such a special word, as by witnesses, we stay with שמואל's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
Because the פסוק says

phrases.english: It is different there,
because the verse says: 'He shall surely be put to death.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The murderer case seemed to show that we never need a פסוק done exactly as written.
steps.terutzMaskana: The murderer is an exception, created by the special words מות יומת.

steps.title: Why not learn a general rule from the murderer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: let us learn from the murderer that in every death penalty, if the written way cannot be done, we use another way.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 17 and sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the murderer is the source, maybe it should teach a rule for all executions. If so, the witnesses case would follow it too, and שמואל's rule would fall again.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us learn from it

phrases.english: But let us learn from it?
phrases.notes: He means: learn from the murderer a rule for every death penalty, including our witnesses case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the murderer is only a special case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule written in one place can often be applied to similar cases, so the murderer case should teach about all executions.

steps.title: Two פסוקים teaching the same thing do not teach a general rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the murderer and the גואל הדם are שני כתובין הבאין כאחד, and such a pair does not teach other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the murderer and the blood-avenger are two פסוקים that come as one, and any two פסוקים that come as one do not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why we cannot learn a general rule from the murderer, which keeps שמואל's rule safe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'any way possible' idea is written twice, once about the murderer and once about the גואל הדם. If it were a rule for everything, the Torah would only need to write it once. Writing it twice shows these are exceptions, so they cannot teach about the witnesses case.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood-avenger, a relative of the person who was killed
Two פסוקים that teach the same idea
They do not teach other cases

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule stands: the 'any way possible' rule by a murderer is a Torah exception, written twice, so it does not spread to other executions.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that two פסוקים make a rule stronger. Here it is the opposite: because the Torah had to say it twice, we learn that it is limited to those two cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: שני כתובין הבאין כאחד אין מלמדין is a basic rule of learning from פסוקים that comes up all over ש״ס.

phrases.english: Because the murderer and the blood-avenger are
two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה רוֹצֵחַ וְגוֹאֵל הַדָּם שְׁנֵי כְּתוּבִין הַבָּאִין כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 and closes this line of challenges to שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rule of learning from פסוקים (שני כתובין הבאין כאחד)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The murderer case might teach a general rule for all executions.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the idea is written by both the murderer and the גואל הדם, it is limited to them and does not teach other cases.

steps.title: Which two verses make up the pair?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the murderer as the first of the two פסוקים and asks what the second one, the גואל הדם, is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The murderer is the case we already said. What is the case of the גואל הדם?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining the 'two verses' it just mentioned in step 19. It says the first one is the murderer, and now sets up the next move by asking what the גואל הדם source is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19 the גמרא said רוצח and גואל הדם are שני כתובין הבאין כאחד. The murderer source is already known from step 16, but we have not yet seen where the גואל הדם teaches 'any way.' This question opens the door for the ברייתא that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'blood redeemer': the relative of the person who was killed, who is given the job of killing the murderer
'This is what we said': pointing back to something already discussed
'What is it?': asking for the source or details

phrases.english: The murderer: this is what we already said.
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא from step 16: if the murderer can't be killed the way the Torah says, he's killed any way possible.

phrases.english: The blood redeemer: what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two פסוקים mentioned in the answer of step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where is the source that the גואל הדם law also works 'in any way' (beyond its written form)?

steps.title: The court appoints a blood redeemer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the מצוה falls on the גואל הדם, and if there is none, בית דין appoints one, learned from 'בפגעו בו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: 'The גואל הדם shall kill the murderer.' The מצוה is on the גואל הדם. And how do we know that if he has no גואל, בית דין appoints one for him? Because it says 'when he meets him,' which means in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא. The פסוק names the relative as the one who kills, but the extra words 'בפגעו בו' teach that even someone appointed by בית דין can do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here, like the murderer, the Torah gives a specific way (the relative) and then adds words that widen it to 'מכל מקום' (any case). So we now have two פסוקים that each teach the same 'any way' idea. That is exactly why, as step 19 said, they cannot be used to teach other death penalties.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As it was taught': introduces a ברייתא
They appoint a redeemer for him
'When he meets him': the words in the פסוק that widen the law
In any case / in any way

steps.whatToRemember: The pair of שני כתובין הבאין כאחד is: the murderer (killed any way possible) and the גואל הדם (even a court-appointed one). Because the Torah needed to say this twice, it does not spread to other death penalties.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"The blood redeemer shall kill the murderer":
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:21

phrases.english: the מצוה is on the blood redeemer.
And from where do we know that if he has no redeemer,
the court appoints a redeemer for him?
As it says: "When he meets him": in any case.
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:21. 'In any case' means even a redeemer the court appoints, not only a relative.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא גֹּאֵל הַדָּם יָמִית אֶת הָרֹצֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 by giving the ברייתא for גואל הדם.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא learns from 'בפגעו בו' that if there is no relative, בית דין appoints a גואל, so the law is carried out in any way.

steps.title: Don't we need the verse exactly as written?
steps.stepSummary: מר קשישא asks רב אשי whether we really require a פסוק to be done as written, citing the משנה that a בן סורר ומורה with a disabled parent is not judged.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר קשישא son of רב חסדא said to רב אשי: Don't we need the פסוק to be done exactly as written? But we learned in a משנה: if one of the parents was missing a hand, or mute, or lame, or blind, or deaf, the boy does not become a בן סורר ומורה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new voice, מר קשישא, raises the general question of whether a פסוק must be carried out exactly as written. He brings a משנה about the rebellious son where tiny details of the פסוק must be met exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 16-19 explored when the Torah's written way may be swapped for another way. מר קשישא points to בן סורר ומורה, where any parent who cannot physically do what the פסוק describes stops the whole law. This suggests that, as a rule, the Torah's words must be done exactly as written.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse exactly as it is written
'But we learned in a משנה': introduces a source used to challenge
The 'stubborn and rebellious son' of דברים פרק כא
Someone missing a hand
Someone who is lame

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר קַשִּׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar Kashisha, son of Rav Chisda, said to Rav Ashi:
And do we not need the verse as it is written?
But didn't we learn: if one of them was missing a hand,
phrases.notes: 'One of them' means one of the boy's parents.

phrases.english: or mute, or lame,
or blind, or deaf,
he does not become a stubborn and rebellious son.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי לָא בָּעֵינַן קְרָא כְּדִכְתִיב וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that the murderer/גואל הדם pair is an exception, a new challenge tests the general principle of following a פסוק exactly.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea from steps 16-19 that the written way of a פסוק can sometimes be replaced with another way.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In בן סורר ומורה even a small physical inability of a parent cancels the whole law, showing that the Torah's words must be met exactly as written.

steps.title: Each disability comes from a word in the verse
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's source: each word of the פסוקים about the rebellious son excludes a different kind of disabled parent.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'They shall grab him': not those missing a hand. 'And bring him out': not the lame. 'And they shall say': not the mute. 'This son of ours': not the blind. 'He does not listen to our voice': not the deaf.
steps.whatsHappening: This is still part of the quoted משנה. It shows how every action in the פסוק (grabbing, bringing out, saying, pointing, being heard) must be physically possible for the parents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase is read very literally: grabbing needs hands, bringing out needs walking, saying needs speech, 'this' needs seeing to point, and 'our voice' needs hearing. This literal reading is what gives מר קשישא's challenge its strength.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they shall grab him'
Mute people
Blind people
Deaf people

phrases.english: As it says: "They shall grab him": and not those missing a hand,
phrases.notes: דברים 21:19

phrases.english: "And they shall bring him out": and not the lame,
"And they shall say": and not the mute,
phrases.notes: דברים 21:20

phrases.english: "This son of ours": and not the blind,
"He does not listen to our voice": and not the deaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק-based source for the משנה quoted in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That a פסוק must be done exactly as written.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's word-by-word reading of דברים 21:19-20 about the בן סורר ומורה.

steps.title: Isn't the reason that we follow the verse exactly?
steps.stepSummary: מר קשישא presses the point: the only reason for this rule must be that a פסוק has to be done as written.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Is it not because we need the פסוק done exactly as written?
steps.whatsHappening: מר קשישא finishes his challenge by pointing out the lesson he sees in the משנה. He says the reason must be the general rule of following a פסוק as written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge moves from one specific case to a general principle. If the reason for the בן סורר ומורה rule is 'קרא כדכתיב', then that principle should apply to every פסוק, including the death penalties discussed before.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
'Is it not because...?': suggests a reason as obvious

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Is it not because we need the verse as it is written?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּבָעֵינַן קְרָא כְּדִכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the general inference from the משנה and its source in steps 22-23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a פסוק's written way need not always be followed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only explanation for the בן סורר ומורה rule is the general principle of קרא כדכתיב, which should then apply everywhere.

steps.title: The rebellious son is special because the whole verse is extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that בן סורר ומורה is different, since that entire פסוק is extra, so it teaches its details strictly only there.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is different there, because the whole פסוק is extra.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects מר קשישא's proof. It says the rebellious son case is special and does not show a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the whole פסוק about grabbing, bringing out, and saying is not needed for its plain meaning, the Torah wrote it to demand every detail exactly. Other פסוקים are not extra like this, so they do not automatically require being done exactly as written.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is different there': the case brought is special
An extra verse, not needed for its basic meaning

steps.whatToRemember: בן סורר ומורה is a special case: because its whole פסוק is extra, every detail must be met exactly. That does not prove that every פסוק must be done exactly as written.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the rebellious son details are unimportant. It is saying they are extra-strict there because the פסוק is extra, so you cannot copy that strictness to other laws.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer separates a special strict case from a general rule, so the בן סורר ומורה rule cannot be used to decide every other פסוק.

phrases.english: No, it is different there,
because the entire verse is extra.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּכוּלֵּיהּ קְרָא יַתִּירָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 22-24 by limiting the בן סורר ומורה rule to its own case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cited case (שאני התם) as a special exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בן סורר ומורה rule proves a general principle that every פסוק must be done exactly as written.
steps.terutzMaskana: The strictness there comes only because that whole פסוק is extra, so it does not set a general rule.

steps.title: A city with no open square
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about an עיר הנדחת that has no open square: רבי ישמעאל says it cannot become an עיר הנדחת, and רבי עקיבא says we make a square for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if the city has no open square, it does not become an עיר הנדחת. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: if it has no open square, we make an open square for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to settle the question of whether a פסוק must be done exactly as written. This step quotes the source, and the next step will draw the proof from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says the spoils of an עיר הנדחת are gathered into the city's open square and burned. The ברייתא asks what happens if the city has no square, and רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא give different answers.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as a proof
A city where most of the people worshipped idols, which is destroyed and burned
The open square of a city

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If it has no open square,
phrases.notes: The פסוק says to gather the city's spoils into its square and burn them (דברים 13:17).

phrases.english: it does not become an idolatrous city;
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהּ רְחוֹב – עוֹשִׂין לָהּ רְחוֹב.
phrases.english: If it has no open square, we make an open square for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from בן סורר ומורה was pushed aside, the גמרא tries a new source on the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That a פסוק must be carried out exactly as written (קרא כדכתיב).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the dispute of רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא about an עיר הנדחת with no square.

steps.title: Both sides need the square the פסוק describes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא only argue about whether the square must exist from the start. Both agree the פסוק must be done as written.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only disagree on this point: one master holds that we need 'its square' as it was from the start, and the other master holds that a square made now also counts like one that was there from the start. But everyone agrees that we need the פסוק to be done exactly as written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof out of the ברייתא. Even רבי עקיבא, who is lenient, still requires a square, so everyone seems to hold קרא כדכתיב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not say the square can be skipped. He says to build one, which shows he also thinks the פסוק's detail cannot be dropped. The only argument is about timing, so the requirement of a square looks unanimous.

keyTerms.meaning: They only argue up to this point; beyond it they agree
From the start; here, at the time of the idol worship
Now
The פסוק must be carried out exactly as it is written

phrases.english: They disagree only to this extent,
that one master holds:
we need 'its square' as it was from the start,
and the other master holds:
a square made now is also like one from the start.
But according to everyone,
we need the verse to be done as it is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי, אֶלָּא דְּמָר סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the actual proof out of the ברייתא quoted in step 26.
steps.raayaObject: That everyone agrees קרא כדכתיב is required.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Even רבי עקיבא requires making a square, so the dispute is only about timing.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים: the מצורע missing a right thumb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that whether a פסוק must be done exactly as written is a dispute between תנאים, as shown by the משנה about a מצורע who lacks a right thumb, big toe, or ear.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים, as we learned: if he has no thumb, no big toe, or no right ear, he can never become pure. רבי אליעזר says: the כהן puts it on the place where the limb should be, and that is enough. רבי שמעון says: he puts it on the left side, and that is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the proof by saying that not everyone agrees. There are תנאים who hold that a פסוק does not have to be done exactly as written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first תנא holds that without the right limb the מצורע can never become pure, which means the פסוק must be done exactly as written. רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון find another way to do it, so in their view the exact detail can be given up when it is impossible. Since this is an open dispute, the עיר הנדחת case cannot prove that everyone holds קרא כדכתיב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
The thumb and the big toe
Purity, ever; here, he can never become pure
And he has fulfilled his obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying the proof from עיר הנדחת was read wrong. It is saying that even if those two תנאים agree, other תנאים disagree, so no rule binds everyone.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether a פסוק must be done exactly as written (קרא כדכתיב) is a dispute between תנאים. The first תנא of the מצורע משנה requires it, while רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון allow a substitute.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of Tannaim,
as we learned in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ בֹּהֶן יָד, בֹּהֶן רֶגֶל, אֹזֶן יָמָנִית –
phrases.english: If he has no thumb, big toe, or right ear,
phrases.notes: This is a מצורע becoming pure. Blood and oil go on his right thumb, right big toe, and right ear (ויקרא 14:14).

phrases.english: he can never become pure.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
He puts it on its place, and he has fulfilled his duty.
Rabbi Shimon says:
He puts it on his left, and he has fulfilled his duty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof of step 27 by showing that the principle is not agreed upon by everyone.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the issue is a dispute between תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both sides in the עיר הנדחת dispute require a square, everyone would seem to hold קרא כדכתיב.
steps.terutzMaskana: קרא כדכתיב is not universal. The first תנא about the מצורע requires it, while רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון do not.

steps.title: New משנה: which executed people are hung
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins: רבי אליעזר says everyone who is stoned is hung after death, while the חכמים say only the מגדף and the עובד עבודה זרה are hung.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: all who are stoned are hung after death. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. The חכמים say: only the one who curses God and the one who worships idols are hung.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new משנה about hanging the body of a person executed by stoning. It records a dispute over who gets hung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר applies hanging to every case of סקילה. The חכמים limit it to two sins, the מגדף and the עובד עבודה זרה, so they treat hanging as belonging only to those cases.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה: the start of a new משנה
People who are executed by stoning (סקילה)
Are hung (the body, after death)
One who curses God

phrases.english: MISHNA:
All who are stoned are hung,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
And the Rabbis say:
None is hung except
the blasphemer and the idol worshipper.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַנִּסְקָלִין נִתְלִין, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins, moving from the question of קרא כדכתיב to the law of hanging after execution.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר holds that all who are stoned are hung. The חכמים hold that only the מגדף and the עובד עבודה זרה are hung.

steps.title: How a man and a woman are hung, and whether a woman is hung at all
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. רבי אליעזר says a man is hung facing the people and a woman is hung facing the tree. The חכמים say a man is hung but a woman is not hung.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man is hung with his face toward the people, and a woman is hung with her face toward the tree. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. The חכמים say: a man is hung, but a woman is not hung.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps going with the same argument from Step 29. Now it argues about women: how they are hung, or whether they are hung at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that a woman is hung too, but she faces the tree for modesty. The חכמים say the hanging is only for a man, so a woman is never hung.

keyTerms.meaning: they hang (the body, after the execution)
facing the people
facing the tree (the wooden post)
she is hung

steps.confusionAlert: This hanging happens only after the person has already been put to death. It is not a way of killing someone.

phrases.english: A man, they hang him
with his face toward the people,
and a woman, with her face toward the tree;
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
And the Sages say:
a man is hung,
but a woman is not hung.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאִישׁ תּוֹלִין אוֹתוֹ פָּנָיו כְּלַפֵּי הָעָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from Step 29 with a second argument about women.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר says a man is hung facing the people and a woman is hung facing the tree. The חכמים say only a man is hung.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר brings proof from שמעון בן שטח
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks the חכמים: didn't שמעון בן שטח hang women in אשקלון? This seems to show that women are hung.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to them: Didn't שמעון בן שטח hang women in אשקלון?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר brings a real event from history to prove that women are hung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question form is really a proof, aimed at the חכמים. If a great leader like שמעון בן שטח hung women, then women must be hung, just as רבי אליעזר said.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't...? (a question that brings proof)
a great leader of the חכמים in the time of the בית שני
אשקלון, a city

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to them:
Didn't Shimon ben Shatach
hang women in Ashkelon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אליעזר supports his opinion from Step 30 against the חכמים.
steps.raayaObject: That a woman's body is hung after execution.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The event when שמעון בן שטח hung women in אשקלון.

steps.title: The חכמים reject the proof: that was not a normal court ruling
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that שמעון בן שטח hung eighty women in one day. A court may not judge two capital cases in one day, so this was a special emergency act. It does not show what the regular law is.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: He hung eighty women, and a court does not judge two people in one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push away רבי אליעזר's proof. They show that the event in אשקלון did not follow the regular rules of the court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By normal law, one court may not judge even two death cases on the same day. Hanging eighty women in one day breaks that rule, so it must have been an emergency step for that time. You cannot learn the regular law from it.

keyTerms.meaning: eighty
they do not judge
in one day

steps.whatToRemember: An emergency act of a court, done outside the normal rules, cannot be used as proof for the regular law.

phrases.english: They said to him:
He hung eighty women,
and a court does not judge two people in one day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי אליעזר's proof from Step 31.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The חכמים agree the event happened, but say it was not a regular court ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The event broke the rule against judging two capital cases in one day, so it was an emergency act and not the normal law.

steps.title: The source for hanging: רבי אליעזר learns from the מגדף that all who are stoned are hung
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the פסוק "והומת ותלית". Someone might think everyone who is executed is hung. The second פסוק, "כי קללת אלהים תלוי", points to the מקלל (the מגדף). רבי אליעזר learns that just as the מקלל is stoned, everyone who is stoned is hung.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: "And he is put to death, and you shall hang him." You might think everyone who is executed is hung. So the פסוק says: "For one who is hung is a curse of God." Just as the one who curses God is stoned, so too everyone who is stoned is hung. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and brings a ברייתא that shows where in the Torah the משנה's argument comes from. This step gives רבי אליעזר's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק sounds like it includes everyone who is executed. The second פסוק narrows it down to someone like the מקלל. רבי אליעזר picks "being stoned" as the shared feature, so every person who is stoned is hung, and no one else.

keyTerms.meaning: the Rabbis taught (this opens a ברייתא)
one might have thought
the פסוק teaches us
one who curses God, the מגדף
stoning

phrases.english: GEMARA. The Rabbis taught:
"And he is put to death, and you shall hang him":
phrases.notes: דברים 21:22

phrases.english: one might think that all who are executed are hung?
So the verse teaches:
"For one who is hung is a curse of God."
phrases.notes: דברים 21:23. The ברייתא reads this as talking about someone who cursed God, the מגדף.

phrases.english: Just as this one who curses is put to death by stoning,
so too everyone who is put to death by stoning is hung.
These are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה ends, the גמרא opens with the source in the פסוקים for רבי אליעזר's view from Step 29.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's rule that everyone who is stoned is hung.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 21:22-23, comparing everyone else to the מקלל.

steps.title: The חכמים learn from the מגדף that only those who deny God are hung
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with the חכמים. They compare to the מקלל too, but they choose a different shared feature: he denied God. So only those who deny God are hung.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: Just as the one who curses God denied the basic belief in God, so too everyone who denied the basic belief in God is hung.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the חכמים's reading of the same פסוק. It explains why they say only the מגדף and the עובד עבודה זרה are hung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides compare to the מקלל. The difference is which feature they copy. For the חכמים it is "denying God," not "being stoned." That leaves only the מגדף and the עובד עבודה זרה, as the משנה said.

keyTerms.meaning: denied the root belief, meaning he denied God

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
Just as this one who curses denied the basic belief in God,
so too everyone who denied the basic belief in God is hung.
phrases.notes: The מגדף and the one who serves idols, the same two the משנה listed in Step 29.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים מָה מְקַלֵּל זֶה שֶׁכָּפַר בָּעִיקָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side's reading of the same פסוק from Step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only those who deny God, meaning the מגדף and the עובד עבודה זרה, are hung.

steps.title: What is the root of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the real reason is that רבי אליעזר and the חכמים read the פסוק differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are they arguing about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next step. It wants to know the deeper cause of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same פסוקים and both compare to the מקלל. So the גמרא wants to know what makes one side pick "stoning" and the other side pick "denying God."

keyTerms.meaning: what are they arguing about?

phrases.english: What are they arguing about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the root of the argument between Steps 33 and 34.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which basic difference in reading the Torah causes the two different comparisons to the מקלל.

steps.title: Two methods of reading the Torah: כלל ופרט versus ריבוי ומיעוט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the חכמים read the Torah using כללי ופרטי (general statements and details), while רבי אליעזר reads it using ריבויי ומיעוטי (widening and narrowing).
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים read the Torah using general statements and details. רבי אליעזר reads it using widening and narrowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 35. The argument comes from two different methods of learning the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under כלל ופרט, the details hold back the general statement tightly. So the rule stays very close to the detail, someone who denied God like the מקלל. Under ריבוי ומיעוט, the narrowing is weaker, so a broader group, everyone who is stoned, is included.

keyTerms.meaning: general statements and details, a method of reading the Torah
widening and narrowing, a different method of reading the Torah
they interpret, they learn out from the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: The argument about who is hung is not only about this law. It comes from two different methods of reading the Torah: the חכמים use כלל ופרט, which gives a tight rule (only those who deny God), and רבי אליעזר uses ריבוי ומיעוט, which gives a wider rule (everyone who is stoned).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a pattern found all over ש״ס. Two opinions can come from one basic choice about how to read the Torah.

phrases.english: The Rabbis interpret using general statements and details,
Rabbi Eliezer interprets using widening and narrowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים use כלל ופרט, which gives a narrow rule. רבי אליעזר uses ריבוי ומיעוט, which gives a wider rule.

steps.title: The חכמים label one phrase as general and the other as a detail
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out how the חכמים read the פסוקים: 'והומת ותלית' is a כלל, and 'כי קללת' is a פרט.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים read the Torah using general statements and details. 'And he is put to death, and you shall hang him' is the general statement. 'For a curse of God' is the detail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is filling in the answer from step 36. It shows exactly which words the חכמים treat as the general statement and which words they treat as the detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 36 only said that the חכמים use כללי ופרטי. Now we learn how that works here. 'והומת ותלית' is the כלל because it speaks about executed people in general. 'כי קללת' is the פרט because it points to one specific case, the מקלל.

keyTerms.meaning: They expound, meaning they interpret the פסוק to learn a law from it
A general statement in the Torah that covers many cases
A detail in the Torah that names one specific case

phrases.english: The Rabbis expound using generalizations and details:
"And he is put to death, and you shall hang him" is a generalization,
phrases.notes: דברים 21:22

phrases.english: "For a curse of God" is a detail.
phrases.notes: דברים 21:23. This is the phrase that points to the מקלל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the answer of step 36 by applying the חכמים' method to the actual words of the פסוקים
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For the חכמים, 'והומת ותלית' is the כלל and 'כי קללת' is the פרט

steps.title: If the general statement and the detail were next to each other, only the detail's case would be hung
steps.stepSummary: If the כלל and the פרט were next to each other, the rule 'אין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט' would apply. Only the מקלל would be hung, and nobody else.
steps.simpleTranslation: If these two phrases were close to each other, we would say: the general statement includes only what is in the detail. This case would be hung, and nothing else would.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states what the normal rule of כלל ופרט would teach if the two phrases stood right next to each other. This is a setup line, because the word 'if' hints that the phrases are actually apart. That gets the next move ready.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the plain rule of כלל ופרט, the detail limits the general statement. Then only the exact case named in the פרט, the מקלל, would be hung. The 'if' tells us this is not yet the final result, because in the Torah these phrases are separated.

keyTerms.meaning: Close to each other, meaning standing right next to each other in the פסוק
The general statement includes only what is in the detail
Yes
Anything else

steps.confusionAlert: Do not take this as the final ruling of the חכמים. It is an 'if' case. In step 34 the חכמים actually include everyone who denied God, which is more than just the מקלל. The גמרא is about to explain how the gap between the phrases changes the result.

phrases.english: If they were close to each other,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִינַן: אֵין בַּכְּלָל אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁבַּפְּרָט.
phrases.english: we would say: the generalization includes only what is in the detail.
These, yes; anything else, no.
phrases.notes: 'These' means the case named in the detail, the מקלל. Only he would be hung.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the standard rule of כלל ופרט to the labels given in step 37, as an 'if' case that sets up the next point
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the כלל and the פרט were next to each other, only the case in the פרט (the מקלל) would be hung, and no one else
